mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financial conditions, as reflected in reduced equity discount rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprise in a restrictive policy regime
failure_condition: Over a 12-month walk-forward period, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative whenever the trigger occurs, or the change in discount rate (measured via 10Y Treasury yield) does not exceed the Fed Funds increase by more than 0.25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate falls below 0.2% for two consecutive months, it predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market expectations for future disinflation reduce equity discounting.
failure_condition: Empirical power of the signal is insignificant (p > 0.05) in regimes where unemployment is above 4%, or the 10-day rolling volatility of SPX exceeds 1.5% during the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) by at least 10,000 jobs in a single month is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong labor demand compresses wage growth and raises inflation expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 in a single month
regime_hint: Labor market tightness during a growth cycle
failure_condition: The effect is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05) after controlling for GDP growth and unemployment rate, or the 20-day returns following the trigger are not meaningfully lower than the prior 20-day average.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (real personal consumption) and HOUST (retail sales) above their prior month's levels by at least 2% each predict a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting robust consumer and business demand momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↑ ≥2% AND HOUST ↑ ≥2% in the same month
regime_hint: Economic expansion with resilient retail and consumption
failure_condition: The interaction coefficient is insignificant (p > 0.05) in recessions (UNRATE < 5%), or the 20-day return is not higher than the average of the 10 days before the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) by more than 5% in a month signals supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as market anticipates slower growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
regime_hint: Industrial production contraction in a non-stagflationary environment
failure_condition: The signal fails to predict negative returns in periods where GDP growth is positive (>1%) or the S&P 500 60-day volatility is below its 5-year median.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market slack diminishes and hiring accelerates.
regime_hint: Approaching full employment in a steady growth regime
failure_condition: The effect is not robust across multiple cycles (backtested across 10 economic expansions), or the 20-day return is not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average in the trigger regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -0.5% for two consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as discounting of future cash flows weakens.
regime_hint: Deflationary monetary policy or weak demand
failure_condition: The signal fails to predict positive returns when GDP growth is negative, or the 10-year real yield does not fall by more than 0.3 percentage points during the same window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in FEDFUNDS and PAYEMS by at least 0.25% and 5,000 jobs, respectively, in the same month indicate a dual contraction in monetary accommodation and labor demand, which predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to heightened risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ↓ ≥0.25% AND PAYEMS ↓ ≥5,000 in the same month
regime_hint: Dual contraction in policy easing and labor market strength
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in periods where the S&P 500 20-day volatility is below its 1-year average, or the 20-day return is not meaningfully lower than the average of the 10 days prior to the trigger.
